correctness.rationale: Translate the first landmark to zero and permute coordinates so the second differs on h coordinates. Count words by their two block weights (i,j), fold their two distances, divide by two for the free antipodal action, then remove the two landmark classes. Interior coordinate counts give at least h per complement orbit away from the central layer; the one possible self-complementary count pair still gives at least h because the second block is larger. Toggling one of the h differing coordinates exhibits the exact smallest class (1,h-1) if 2<=h<n/2. For h=1 each nonlandmark pair has an interior second-block count, so its product of binomial factors is at least n-1; the class (1,2) attains this. Line 45's literal wording about 'a binomial factor equal to one' is imprecise (the first factor is always one); the product and the intended bound are as just shown. For even n=2m and h=m, if both block counts are interior the orbit count is at least m^2, except the halved central count which is still at least 2m for even m>=4. When one is an endpoint, swapping the two blocks gives a disjoint complement orbit of size at least m with the same signature. The neighbors of a attain 2m. At n=4 the self-complementary class contributes the exceptional two vertices. The resulting comparison across h proves the optimizing separations; shell sizes n and half the central binomial coefficient give the claimed unordered-pair counts.
